overall_quality.evidence: Object-oriented programming (OOP) is a programming paradigm that emphasizes the use of objects to design software. The principles of OOP include encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism. Encapsulation involves bundling data and methods that operate on that data into a single unit called a class. Inheritance allows classes to inherit properties and methods from other classes, promoting code reuse. Polymorphism enables objects to be treated as instances of their parent class, allowing for flexible and extensible code.
